parsed.explanation: The combined regime documents no trans-specific criminal offence (2022 decriminalisation), no entry or document rules targeting trans visitors, and no documented detention, violence, or facility restrictions — so no tier-1 or tier-2 exposure is proven. But the dossier is thin on enforcement, and its structural signals cut against safety: discrimination and hate speech remain lawful with no statutory remedy, and 2025 civil-society reporting states LGBTQ+ people avoid law enforcement, making police an unreliable protection route. Official hostility is documented (2005 port exclusion, 2011 'no mandate' statement), though both are dated and pre-decriminalisation. Sodomy-law repeal was litigation-driven and potentially reversible. No criminalisation plus documented hostility with thin recourse yields mid-scale, not Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: No immigration or visa rule singling out trans travellers is sourced. The 2005 port exclusion of an LGBTQ cruise ship was ad hoc and 20 years old, not a published entry rule.
entry_documents.protection: Travellers use home-jurisdiction documents that cannot be altered locally; no document-mismatch rule is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at the border is an open question, not a documented exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. Prosecution, police and court practice toward gender-nonconforming people after 2022 is explicitly unsourced.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Consensual same-sex conduct decriminalised nationally since 2022 via constitutional ruling; no trans-specific criminal offence documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Regional litigation can shift the position without domestic political change, so durability is uncertain.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, custody-placement or strip-search rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence reflects thin reporting, not confirmed safety.

care_services.exposure: No documented care denial; discrimination in services lawful with no remedy.
care_services.protection: National gender equality policy 2022-2027 names LGBTQ+ people, but civil society reports no tangible steps.
care_services.interaction: Paper policy without implementation offers a traveller no operational protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2025 civil-society submission: LGBTQ+ people avoid law enforcement — police are not a reliable protection route. Official hostility documented in 2005 port exclusion and 2011 'no mandate' statement, both dated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: LGBTI organisations may register; decriminalisation succeeded through constitutional challenge.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing plus unreliable police means harassment has thin recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific or guardian-specific rule documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family-travel exposure not addressed by sources; extrapolate from general thin-recourse posture.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence or hate-crime data exists; no general homicide comparison available. Discrimination and hate speech remain lawful.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented trans killings or organised targeting.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police avoidance means even a documented assault would face unreliable response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or harassment statute; no post-repeal successor protection. Victim of service refusal has no local statutory remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional court demonstrated willingness to strike rights-violating provisions; LGBTI orgs can operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Constitutional route exists in principle but no documented relief for trans visitors.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.45-D rests on mandatory registration and nightly hotel-to-database transmission — a documented universal exposure. This dossier documents no registration, database, or checkpoint regime, so it sits above 0.45-D despite comparably thin recourse and official coolness.

0.55-B has documented border secondary screening and discretionary refusal of entry. Here no entry-stage exposure is sourced at all, but comparable administrative opacity, dated official hostility and police avoidance keep the case from rising toward 0.65 — similar level, different composition.

0.65-C shows courts and clinics actually delivering remedies (injunction, damages, fine). This dossier shows courts delivering only decriminalisation, while discrimination stays lawful and LGBTQ+ people avoid police — remedies do not operate, so it sits a clear step below 0.65-C.

parsed.synthesis: The regime decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2022 and documents no trans-specific offence, no entry rule, and no facility or custody exposure — the absence of any tier-1 or tier-2 feature keeps it out of the lower bands. Against that, discrimination and hate speech are lawful with no statutory remedy, a 2025 civil-society submission says LGBTQ+ people avoid law enforcement (so police protection is unreliable if a traveller is harassed or assaulted), and official hostility is documented though dated (2005 port exclusion, 2011 'no mandate'). Enforcement practice after 2022 is unsourced and repeal came via regional litigation that can shift without domestic political change. Silence here is thin-data, not safety: extrapolating from decriminalisation plus absent protections plus police avoidance yields mid-scale — reduced criminal exposure, but hostility with thin recourse.
